intended_object: For an isomorphism α : X ≅ Y in a category C and any object Z, the bijection Hom(Z, X) ≃ Hom(Z, Y) given by postcomposition with α (f ↦ f ≫ α.hom), with inverse postcomposition with α⁻¹. The docstring and name say this.
explanation: The forward map is f ↦ f ≫ α.hom and the inverse is g ↦ g ≫ α.inv. They are inverse to each other because α.hom ≫ α.inv = 𝟙 and α.inv ≫ α.hom = 𝟙, and the `cat_disch` proofs check exactly this. This is the standard bijection on hom-sets that an isomorphism induces, i.e. the Yoneda functor applied to α, evaluated at Z. The setting is fully general: any category, any universe levels, any objects. Nothing is missing and nothing is more special than it needs to be. The declaration is Mathlib's own basic version of this construction, so there is no separate counterpart to cite. Its dual, `homFromEquiv`, is generated automatically by `to_dual`.
